findings.claim: The os.Chmod that restores the source mode runs after durable.WriteFile has already synced the file, and no later fsync covers the file inode. syncDirectories syncs only directory entries, so after a crash the copy can survive with the umask-derived mode rather than the source mode. That is the very property the commit says it keeps (restoring does not change who can read a page). Chmod before the durable write, or sync the file after the chmod.

evidence: Diff-only review. The write, chmod and directory-sync ordering in copyInto/syncDirectories was read directly from the changed lines.
The source mode is taken from a separate os.Stat after os.ReadFile, so the data and the mode can come from different moments. This is minor and not reported as a finding.
The tests cover the mode, the mid-copy write failure, the failed cleanup and the third backup at one instant. None covers the durability of the chmod.
